investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Available Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-16T10:57–11:04Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: 0/6 nodes are available, 2 nodes reporting Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm and 4 nodes not matching the pod's node affinity/selector. The Kubernetes cluster could not schedule the eval's remote agent pod, so the agent never reached a ready state and no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was produced, causing the expected-output contract to fail completely.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the two nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. The remaining four nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints at all. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on the two eligible nodes. As a result, every remote-agent pod submitted during the eval window was stuck Unschedulable for 130–150 seconds before the probe timed out, and no VM was ever assigned, so vmIdPresent and remoteState were never populated. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.' — the scheduler explicitly names kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion on the only two affinity-eligible nodes.
failed-check.timing: status=fail latencyMs=134984 — the probe ran for ~135 s before failing, consistent with a pod stuck unscheduled for 131 s as stated in the message.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical Unschedulable message, latencyMs=151368, endedAt=2026-07-16T11:02:05.941Z — a separately submitted pod for the state check hit the same capacity wall.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical Unschedulable message, latencyMs=150422, endedAt=2026-07-16T11:04:36.363Z — a third independently submitted pod also failed to schedule.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent — consistent with the agent pod never starting and the runner never reaching the evidence-write path in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs lines 1884–1885.
failed-check.evidence: empty object {} — no evidence was captured at all, confirming the runner aborted before any API response was received.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885; if the resulting pod cannot be scheduled, the agent creation call never resolves successfully and no evidence keys are written.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots exhausted on the two affinity-eligible nodes: the scheduler message explicitly states 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on 2/6 nodes with no preemption victims available, leaving zero schedulable capacity for new remote-agent pods at the time of the eval run.

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4/6 nodes: four cluster nodes are structurally ineligible for remote-agent pods (wrong label, taint, or zone), reducing the effective scheduling pool to only the two kata-capable nodes. If those two nodes are at capacity, the entire feature is blocked.

TERTIARY — concurrent remote-agent workloads consuming all kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: if other production or eval workloads were running remote agents simultaneously, they may have consumed all available VM slots before the eval pods were submitted, causing transient exhaustion rather than a permanent capacity deficit.

QUATERNARY — cluster node count or kata-peerpods node pool has not scaled to meet demand: the pool may be under-provisioned relative to the number of concurrent remote-agent pods the system is expected to support.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api between 10:59 and 11:04 UTC on 2026-07-16 with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: 0/6 nodes are available, 2 nodes reporting Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm and 4 nodes not matching the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the eval pod could not be scheduled, the agent was never created, and the remote-agent-state check received zero evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state all missing), causing a full contract violation.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted the allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. The remaining 4 nodes do not match the required affinity/selector at all. With no preemption victims available and no matching nodes with free capacity, every new remote-agent pod is left Unschedulable. This is an infrastructure-layer resource exhaustion localized to the production-api Kubernetes cluster's peer-pod VM pool, not a code defect in the eval runner or the API itself. This is an eval-detected infrastructure failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a label or taint that only 2 nodes carry. If those 2 nodes are also at capacity, the effective schedulable pool is zero regardless of total cluster size.

Tertiary — cluster autoscaler not provisioning new kata-capable nodes in time: if autoscaling is configured, it may not have added a new peer-pod-capable node before the eval's scheduling window expired.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Available Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-16T10:57–11:04Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: 0/6 nodes are available, 2 nodes reporting Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm and 4 nodes not matching the pod's node affinity/selector. The Kubernetes cluster could not schedule the eval's remote agent pod, so the agent never reached a ready state and no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was produced, causing the expected-output contract to fail completely.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots on the two nodes that match the pod's node affinity/selector. The remaining four nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints at all. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on the two eligible nodes. As a result, every remote-agent pod submitted during the eval window was stuck Unschedulable for 130–150 seconds before the probe timed out, and no VM was ever assigned, so vmIdPresent and remoteState were never populated. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
proof: failed-check.message: '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.' — the scheduler explicitly names kata.peerpods.io/vm exhaustion on the only two affinity-eligible nodes.
failed-check.timing: status=fail latencyMs=134984 — the probe ran for ~135 s before failing, consistent with a pod stuck unscheduled for 131 s as stated in the message.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical Unschedulable message, latencyMs=151368, endedAt=2026-07-16T11:02:05.941Z — a separately submitted pod for the state check hit the same capacity wall.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical Unschedulable message, latencyMs=150422, endedAt=2026-07-16T11:04:36.363Z — a third independently submitted pod also failed to schedule.

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all four required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent — consistent with the agent pod never starting and the runner never reaching the evidence-write path in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs lines 1884–1885.
failed-check.evidence: empty object {} — no evidence was captured at all, confirming the runner aborted before any API response was received.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885; if the resulting pod cannot be scheduled, the agent creation call never resolves successfully and no evidence keys are written.
possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots exhausted on the two affinity-eligible nodes: the scheduler message explicitly states 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on 2/6 nodes with no preemption victims available, leaving zero schedulable capacity for new remote-agent pods at the time of the eval run.

SECONDARY — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4/6 nodes: four cluster nodes are structurally ineligible for remote-agent pods (wrong label, taint, or zone), reducing the effective scheduling pool to only the two kata-capable nodes. If those two nodes are at capacity, the entire feature is blocked.

TERTIARY — concurrent remote-agent workloads consuming all kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: if other production or eval workloads were running remote agents simultaneously, they may have consumed all available VM slots before the eval pods were submitted, causing transient exhaustion rather than a permanent capacity deficit.

QUATERNARY — cluster node count or kata-peerpods node pool has not scaled to meet demand: the pool may be under-provisioned relative to the number of concurrent remote-agent pods the system is expected to support.

investigations.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api between 10:59 and 11:04 UTC on 2026-07-16 with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: 0/6 nodes are available, 2 nodes reporting Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm and 4 nodes not matching the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the eval pod could not be scheduled, the agent was never created, and the remote-agent-state check received zero evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state all missing), causing a full contract violation.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted the allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. The remaining 4 nodes do not match the required affinity/selector at all. With no preemption victims available and no matching nodes with free capacity, every new remote-agent pod is left Unschedulable. This is an infrastructure-layer resource exhaustion localized to the production-api Kubernetes cluster's peer-pod VM pool, not a code defect in the eval runner or the API itself. This is an eval-detected infrastructure failure; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

Add a pre-flight scheduling check to the remote-agent eval suite that verifies at least one node with the required affinity/selector has free kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity before attempting agent creation, producing a clearer SKIP or WARN result instead of a timeout-driven FAIL.

Add a leaked-pod detection eval that counts Pending or Terminating remote-agent pods older than a configurable threshold and alerts if any are found, catching resource-holding leaks before they exhaust the pool.

Add a node-affinity coverage eval that asserts the number of nodes matching the remote-agent pod's affinity/selector is above a minimum threshold (e.g., at least 2 healthy nodes), catching pool shrinkage due to node failures or label changes.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes Pod Unschedulable Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes cluster was rejected as Unschedulable: the two nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining four nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No remote agent VM could be provisioned, so the eval runner never received any response evidence, leaving all five required contract fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) absent.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the two eligible nodes. With 0/6 nodes available — 2 reporting Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm and 4 failing node affinity/selector matching — no remote agent pod can be scheduled. The eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1918) therefore never completes, the probe times out after ~150 s, and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-runtime receives zero evidence. This is an eval-infrastructure / cluster-capacity failure localized to the remote-agents Swarm VM pool; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the two eligible nodes: the scheduler message explicitly states 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on 2/6 nodes, meaning the VM slot quota is fully consumed by existing workloads or leaked pods.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4/6 nodes do not match the pod's affinity rules, reducing the schedulable pool to only the 2 kata-capable nodes. If affinity rules changed or nodes were relabeled, the effective capacity could have dropped to zero even with some VM slots free.

Tertiary — leaked or zombie remote-agent pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots: if prior eval runs or user sessions left pods in a non-terminating state, those pods would continue to consume VM resource allocations and prevent new scheduling.
Quaternary — cluster under-provisioning: the total kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity across the 2 eligible nodes may be too small to absorb concurrent eval probe runs alongside normal workloads.

recommendedNextActions: Inspect the Kubernetes cluster immediately for Pending or non-terminating pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots — force-delete any leaked pods from prior eval runs or user sessions to free capacity.

Check the total kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity on the two eligible nodes against current demand; if capacity is structurally insufficient, provision additional kata-capable nodes or increase the VM slot quota.

Review node labels and the remote agent pod's nodeSelector/affinity rules to confirm whether the 4/6 node exclusion is intentional; if nodes were relabeled unintentionally, restore correct labels to expand the schedulable pool.
Add a cluster-level alert for kata.peerpods.io/vm utilization approaching 100% on eligible nodes so capacity exhaustion is detected before it causes eval failures.

Review the eval runner's cleanup logic in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (the withCleanup wrapper at line 1916) to confirm that remote agent pods are reliably terminated after each probe run, preventing slot leakage across runs.

Note that remote-agent-runtime is registered as required=false in infra/evals/status/features.json line 185, so this failure does not by itself trigger an outage classification — but remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state are required=true (lines 183-184) and are also failing, which should be treated with higher urgency.

whatWouldDisproveThis: A successful pod scheduling event on the cluster during the same time window would disprove that kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity was globally exhausted.

Cluster metrics showing kata.peerpods.io/vm slots available and unused on the two eligible nodes at the time of the eval run would suggest the cause is a misconfigured resource request or affinity rule rather than capacity exhaustion.

A passing run of remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, or remote-agent-runtime in the same production-api environment shortly after the failure would indicate a transient burst condition rather than a sustained capacity problem.

Evidence that the 4/6 nodes failing affinity matching were recently relabeled or that the pod spec's node selector was recently changed would shift the primary cause to affinity misconfiguration rather than VM slot exhaustion.
Presence of no Pending or zombie pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots would weaken the leaked-pod hypothesis.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check that probes kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used capacity on all eligible nodes and warns when utilization exceeds a configurable threshold (e.g., 80%), before pod scheduling failures occur.

Add a Pending-pod sentinel eval that detects remote-agent pods stuck in Pending state for more than a configurable duration and reports the scheduler reason, enabling earlier detection of scheduling exhaustion.
Add a post-run cleanup verification eval that confirms no remote-agent pods remain in Running or Pending state after each probe cycle, catching slot leakage before it accumulates.

Consider a node-affinity coverage eval that verifies the number of nodes matching the remote agent pod's affinity rules meets a minimum threshold, alerting if the eligible pool shrinks below a safe floor.
